title: 1. Generative trees
text: Given two converged tree traces, SampleStableTrees() draws fixed, append-sample: trees runs interleaved (chains contribute first draw) strided, tree_k fixed function k – raising sample size later appends new trees, never redraws existing ones. Convergence checked first via TreeESS(), topological effective-sample-size diagnostic (lower Frechet-correlation median-pseudo ESS statistics; Fabreti & Hohna 2022; Magee et al. 2024) used throughout Smith (2026): stride = 11 large enough consecutive draws interleaved pool effectively independent; SampleStableTrees() errors informatively larger sample requested trace supports, rather silently reusing correlated draws.
code: runFiles <- result$runFiles trees250 <- SampleStableTrees(runFiles, nTrees = 250, stride = 11)

what: Continuous data: principal components and distance
title: 3. PCA, alignment and distances
text: continuous characters, prcomp() (base R) already everything needed: Smith (2026) centres character mean, without rescaling unit variance, computes Euclidean distance () first two principal components (Raskin et al. 2026’s pipeline); (ii) principal components (equivalent distance original scaled characters); (iii) additive (squared-Euclidean) distance, appropriate neighbour-joining expected squared distance taxa Brownian motion proportional tree (patristic) distance: Discrete characters get analogous additive fix via CorrectedDistanceMS() (per-character-state-size Jukes-Cantor correction; reduces familiar binary correction every character two states), compared plain HammingDistance():
code: set.seed(1) M <- SimulateContinuous(truth, nChar = 100) scores <- prcomp(M)$x  dPipeline <- dist(scores[, 1:2]) # Raskin et al. (2026)'s pipeline dAllPC <- dist(scores) # all dimensions retained dAdditive <- SquaredEuclideanDistance(scores) # the additive fix mongleFile <- system.file("extdata", "mongle_2023.nex", package = "phyloPCA") stateProportions <- MongleStateProportions(mongleFile) X <- SimulateDiscreteMS(truth, nChar = 100, stateProportions = stateProportions) dHamming <- HammingDistance(X) dCorrected <- CorrectedDistanceMS(X)

title: 3. PCA, alignment and distances
text: Landmark configurations must superimposed (aligned) coordinates comparable taxa. phyloPCA provides two alignments, dependency-free, pure-R implementations: ProcrustesAlign(): ordinary least-squares generalized Procrustes analysis (GPA) – centre, scale unit centroid size, iteratively rotate onto evolving consensus. Equivalent geomorph::gpagen() complete landmark data. RftraAlign(): resistant-fit (RFTRA) superimposition (Siegel & Benson 1982; Slice 1996) – repeated-median scale Tukey-bisquare reweighted rotation, small number grossly displaced landmarks (“Pinocchio effect”: Palci & Lee 2019) -weighted rather smeared across whole configuration. alignments return named list landmarks x dim matrices, order supplied. compute distance neighbour-joining, flatten aligned configuration one row per taxon: alignment better depends shape kernel: Smith (2026) finds Procrustes RFTRA barely distinguishable practice (LDDMM deformations used smooth distributed, without isolated “Pinocchio” landmark outliers RFTRA designed resist), noticeably better superimposition shape kernel sufficiently integrated (see vignette("scoring--figures") shape_sigma_nj_align/score_native/score_rftra datasets, compare three). Continuing worked example scored neighbour-joining tree shown next, vignette("tree-inference").
code: sampleFile <- system.file("extdata", "sample_shape_t00_d2_s0.4.tsv", package = "phyloPCA") configs <- ReadShapeConfigs(sampleFile, dim = 2)[truth$tip.label] # order to tree tips aligned <- ProcrustesAlign(configs) alignedRftra <- RftraAlign(configs) flat <- t(sapply(aligned, function(z) c(z))) dShape <- dist(flat)

title: 5. Scoring reconstructions and reproducing the figures
text: ScoreToTruth() computes three tree-distance metrics used Smith (2026): clustering information distance (CID; Smith 2020, primary metric – normalized 0-1, ~0.84 expected random 21-tip trees), Robinson-Foulds distance (comparability Raskin et al. 2026), (trees strictly binary) SPR distance. ExactlyRecovered() reports (strict, 21 tips) binary criterion exact topology match: OptimalityRecovery() implements alternative, parsimony-specific recovery criterion used maximum-parsimony arms: whether generative tree tied parsimonious, rather whether search happened find – heuristic search’s failure locate true topology among several equally-parsimonious trees counted parsimony criterion .
code: data(generative_trees) truth <- generative_trees[[1]] guess <- ape::rtree(21, tip.label = truth$tip.label) # a random tree, for illustration  ScoreToTruth(guess, truth, metrics = c("CID", "RF")) #>        CID         RF  #>  0.8390693 34.0000000 ExactlyRecovered(guess, truth) #> [1] FALSE

title: 5. Scoring reconstructions and reproducing the figures
text: Figure 1 Smith (2026) compares five ways reconstructing tree continuous character matrices: PCA -> neighbour-joining pipeline (Raskin et al. 2026’s method), neighbour-joining principal components, neighbour-joining additive (squared-Euclidean) distance, maximum parsimony, Bayesian inference. simplified, base-graphics version comparison, drawn directly cached data:  pipeline arm (Raskin et al. 2026’s method) clear outlier; correcting distance fed neighbour-joining (additive arm) recovers essentially gap Bayesian inference, without changing reconstruction method .
code: arms <- c(pipeline = "PCA -> NJ", allpc = "NJ, all PCs",           additive = "NJ, additive", mp = "Parsimony", bayes = "Bayesian") col <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#D55E00", "#000000")  meanBy <- function(arm) {   d <- scale_fig1_dists[scale_fig1_dists$arm == arm, ]   sapply(split(d$CID, d$nC), mean) } nC <- sort(unique(scale_fig1_dists$nC)) plot(NA, xlim = range(nC), ylim = c(0, 0.35), log = "x", las = 1,      xlab = "Number of characters", ylab = "Mean CID to true tree") for (i in seq_along(arms)) {   lines(nC, meanBy(names(arms)[i]), col = col[i], lwd = 2, type = "b", pch = 16) } legend("topright", legend = arms, col = col, lwd = 2, pch = 16, bty = "n")

title: 4. Tree inference: neighbour-joining, parsimony, Bayesian
text: RunTNTParsimony() runs unified search protocol validated across every parsimony arm Smith (2026): 50 random-addition-sequence + TBR starting trees, New Technology pass (sectorial search, ratchet, drift, tree fusing – confirms rather improves RAS+TBR optimum ), TBR-swaps every optimal tree completion saves -parsimonious trees. type = "continuous" treats data Wagner-optimized real-valued characters (Goloboff et al. 2006); "discrete" standard (Fitch) unordered characters; "landmark" linear-displacement-optimized landmark configurations (Goloboff & Catalano’s method, following Palci & Lee 2019). needs local TNT installation (options(phyloPCA.tnt = ...) TNT_PATH environment variable; see FindTNT()) – available vignette built, chunk shown run: search finds one -parsimonious tree (routine discrete shape data), strict consensus -conservative – ScoreMPTsByMaxEntropy() instead takes maximum-entropy subsample k trees (via MaxMin::MaxEntropy(), using clustering information distance measure redundancy trees) reports mean distance truth.
code: result <- RunTNTParsimony(M, type = "continuous") result$nTree # essentially always 1 for continuous (real-valued) data ScoreMPTsByMaxEntropy(result$trees, truth)

title: 4. Tree inference: neighbour-joining, parsimony, Bayesian
text: RunRevBayesBM() RunRevBayesMk() run two-run, Metropolis-coupled Bayesian analyses used throughout Smith (2026): Brownian motion model (dnPhyloBrownianREML) continuous/shape data, per-state-size Mk model discrete data. stop Gelman-Rubin PSRF falls 1.01 parameter ESS exceeds 333. needs local RevBayes installation (see FindRevBayes()) takes order minute even small example – available vignette built, chunk shown run: RunRevBayesMk() works way, discrete-character Nexus file (WriteDiscreteNexus()) instead.
code: nexusFile <- tempfile(fileext = ".nex") WriteContinuousNexus(M, nexusFile) outputPrefix <- tempfile("bm") result <- RunRevBayesBM(nexusFile, outputPrefix, seed = 1) result$mapTrees  mapTree <- ReadMAPTree(result$mapTrees[1]) ScoreToTruth(mapTree, truth, metrics = c("CID", "RF"))

title: phyloPCA
text: Simulating scoring data needs R dependencies (CRAN, plus MaxMin treess, installed automatically Remotes). Reproducing maximum-parsimony Bayesian-inference arms scratch additionally needs TNT RevBayes installed locally – see vignette("tree-inference"). Regenerating geometric-morphometric shape data needs Raskin et al. (2026)’s LDDMM shape simulator, package vendor (repository carries license) – see vignette("simulating-data").

title: phyloPCA
text: Simulation: continuous characters Brownian motion (SimulateContinuous()), multistate discrete characters Mk model (SimulateDiscreteMS()), readers externally-simulated geometric-morphometric shape data (ReadShapeConfigs()). Alignment: dependency-free generalized Procrustes analysis (ProcrustesAlign()) resistant-fit superimposition (RftraAlign()) shape data. Distances: additive (“squaring”) fix neighbour-joining continuous (SquaredEuclideanDistance()) discrete (CorrectedDistanceMS()) data. Tree inference: wrappers maximum-parsimony search TNT (RunTNTParsimony(), continuous/discrete/landmark data, using unified search protocol validated throughout reply) Bayesian inference RevBayes (RunRevBayesBM(), RunRevBayesMk()). Scoring: tree-distance metrics (ScoreToTruth(): clustering information distance, Robinson-Foulds, SPR), exact-match optimality-based recovery (ExactlyRecovered(), OptimalityRecovery()), maximum-entropy subsampling tied -parsimonious trees (ScoreMPTsByMaxEntropy()). Cached results: 250 generative trees (generative_trees) every dataset behind reply’s figures (scale, scale_fig1_dists, shape_combine_nj, others – see vignette("scoring--figures") help(package = "phyloPCA") full list). Bundling means reply’s results can inspected re-plotted without re-running underlying HPC-scale simulation grids.

title: Additive distance for a mixed-state-space discrete matrix — CorrectedDistanceMS
text: Jukes-Cantor-style corrected distance matrix whose characters may different state-space sizes: within observed state-space size k, JC-k correction applied observed proportion differing, expected substitutions summed across state-size blocks expressed per character. Reduces standard binary correction -0.5 * log(1 - 2p) every character k = 2 states. additive distance appropriate neighbour-joining discrete data, mirroring squared-Euclidean fix used continuous data (see SquaredEuclideanDistance()).
